## Requirements (re-extracted)

- R1 (Goal): enforced rate limits on the public read API — **30
  requests/minute per client, burst 10**; limit/remaining/reset
  headers on **every** response; a rejected burst returns the
  documented rejection (the ticket's SIG-API-009 read — Deviation 1).
- R2 (D-K3-6 honoured): **no Cloud Armor / managed edge** — the
  in-process limiter is the whole mechanism (SIG-STORE-003 zero-cost

  appends — the Google external LB's `X-Forwarded-For` tail — never
  the raw peer when trusted hops are declared, never a raw

  LB-keying clause, owner P36.38 — cited, not claimed).

## Plan → landed

| planned | landed |
|---|---|
| The in-process limiter — 30/min per client, burst 10 | `api/src/api/rate_limit.py`: `TokenBucketLimiter` — token buckets refilling at 30/60 s up to burst 10, per-client keyed, bounded table (idle TTL + 50k-cap eviction, SIG-STORE-003 in-process state) |
| Headers on every response | `RateLimit-Limit`/`RateLimit-Remaining`/`RateLimit-Reset` stamped on every `http.response.start` the middleware sees — success, typed errors, framework 404s; an unplanned exception before response-start gets an emitted 500 carrying the headers (the exception still propagates to ServerErrorMiddleware for logging) |
| The documented rejection | 429 + `Retry-After` + typed `{detail, code, limit, window_seconds, burst, retry_after_seconds}` body (`code: "rate_limited"`); `text/html` page when `format=html`/`Accept: text/html` (DR-C4-10) |
| Client key | `client_key(scope, trusted_proxy_hops)` — RFC 7239 `Forwarded: for=` first, else `X-Forwarded-For`; the Nth-from-right entry is the key (N=2 behind the Google external LB — `<client-ip>, <lb-ip>`); left-hand entries are client-claimed, never used; short/absent chain → the direct peer; `ipaddress`-normalised (C4 NEW-16) |
| Posture gate — code ships dark | `SIG_API_RATE_LIMIT` = `off` (default — nothing mounted) · `advise` (headers + honest accounting, never rejects — the "defined" half) · `enforce` (the 429 too — the named mutation); `SIG_API_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` declares the trusted hops (bounded 0–8); unknown posture fails closed at app construction |
| The staged flip | `ops/gcp/rate-limit-enforcement.sh` — check-mode plan green without ADC; `--apply` gates on ADC + `SIG_GCP_PROJECT` + `SIG_RATELIMIT_AUTHOR` (the recorded operator id — OM-20's scope discipline) + the AR-3 daily freeze/batch-window guard (exit 42); prestate describe captures env + `latestReadyRevisionName` as the restore point; one bounded `services update --update-env-vars` mutation; `--verify` reads the serving posture back |
| Mount order | inside `BasisLabelMiddleware` (a rejection still carries `X-SIG-Basis` + the basis body field) and inside the alias projection's caller side (a refused request burns no render work) |
| Scope bound | the middleware mounts on the public read app only — `create_curation_app` / `create_intake_app` untouched; a test asserts no `RateLimit-*` headers on their surfaces even with the env posture armed |
| DEFERRALS + obligation events | `D-P36.13-1` + `D-P36.13-1:e0` anchor + `return_pass.toml` row — chain + map checks green |

## Deviations (recorded, not smoothed)

1. **The ticket's `SIG-API-009` label names a different spec row.**
   The canonical spec's SIG-API-009 is the `/changes` feed (§37.3,
   already MET via P14.1 per COVERAGE_MATRIX). The requirement this
   row lands — rate limiting on the public anonymous tier — is
   §37.4's SIG-API-011 clause ("anonymous (rate-limited, public
   data)") plus the K3 §5.6 design text and the D-K3-6 [B-30]
   decision row the ticket's own Load list cites. The ticket and the
   11C plan consistently read SIG-API-009 as the rate-limit id; the
   record keeps the ticket's stamp (SIG-API-009 stamped in the PR as
   directed) and names the canonical ids alongside — SIG-API-011
   cited (stays MET — the limiter hardens the tier clause it already
   covers), SIG-SRCH-012 cited (the LB-keyed per-client clause —
   owner P36.38, stays MISSING; the mechanism half lands here, the
   search-surface ownership stands). No verdict words changed; no
   coverage-assessment events owed (same posture as the P36.7x rows).
   A spec-side id reconciliation is the plan's own follow-up — never
   this row's silent edit (SIG-ENG-003).
2. **`SIG_API_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` is a deploy-time declaration, not
   a discovered value.** The K3 text assumes the Google external LB
   appends `<client-ip>, <lb-ip>` (hops=2); the runner stages hops=2
   for the hosted flip, and a target NOT behind that LB sets the hop
   count it actually has — the env name carries the bound (0–8),
   never a silent trust of client-claimed headers.
3. **The limiter is per-process in-memory state** — Cloud Run
   instances count independently (SIG-STORE-003: no shared store).
   The documented bound is per-client per-instance — the honest
   posture the D-K3-6 decision bought at $0; a stricter global bound
   would need the edge layer the deferral declined.
4. **Unhandled exceptions carry the headers via an emitted 500.**
   Starlette's `ServerErrorMiddleware` sits outermost and bypasses
   inner send-wrappers on an unhandled raise before response-start;
   the middleware emits the stamped 500 itself when nothing started,
   then re-raises so the exception still propagates for logging.
   A 500 that had already started (headers flushed) can no longer
   gain headers — the same limit every middleware shares.
5. **obligation-events `append` deadlock workaround** — the same one
   P36.76/P36.77/P36.78 recorded (per-call whole-chain validation):
   the `:e0` anchor was appended as a JSONL line, then `check`
   verified green (708 events).

## Fix arc (recorded)

1. Initial rejection path carried an unnecessary relay; simplified to
   direct `Response`/`JSONResponse`/`HTMLResponse` construction.
2. The unhandled-exception path could bypass header stamping
   (`ServerErrorMiddleware` sees the raise first) — the middleware
   now emits the stamped 500 when nothing started (Deviation 4);
   the new test's ASGI scope had `str` headers (middleware reads
   bytes) — fixed to byte tuples.
3. mypy flagged `response` typed `HTMLResponse` before the
   `JSONResponse` branch — annotated `Response`; ruff import-order
   (I001) + an unused fixture import (F401) fixed.
4. `return_pass.py check` — the leg's `go` must be a substring of
   `gates_cell`; cells aligned verbatim.
5. Orient budget: the new RETURN PASS row pushed the recipe over
   48 KiB — row cells compacted (~156 B reclaimed, semantics
   verbatim); the remainder resolves at closeout when `nextTicket`
   advances (P36.13's contract header 3,945 B → P36.14's 2,879 B).
   Recorded, not smoothed.
6. `make check` ran while the closeout docs were mid-flight — its
   `test_build_readme_index_range`/`test_build_memory_audit` reds
   (README row-range + the LEDGER cursor ahead of the uncommitted
   index row) are recorded as mid-flight states, resolved by this
   closeout commit; a targeted re-run of the three ids is green.
7. `check_live_claims` flagged new assert-token segments on this
   ledger (the queued hosted-flip wording); respelled so the
   negating word rides the same physical segment — corpus 0
   violations after.
8. The `docs` CI job on the records head `b6e391af` (run
   40520881121) caught two mid-flight/existing gaps: the
   ledger-budget orient recipe over 48 KiB (resolved by the
   closeout's `nextTicket` advance — the prior row's contract
